As much fun as i had so far, i can't shake off the feeling that this game should've stayed in the oven and in playtests for another year or two. It's very VERY unfinished and unpolished, that was kinda to be expected, but still... i expected a little more of both after the long delay, especially since it's clearly built on the already existing DRG framework. Now... to the most common pain points:

[b] The timer and Incursions [/b]

My main issue here is not the timer itself, but how the distractions the game throws at you affect it. Needing to manage your time efficiently, estimating what you will be able to complete based on cave complexity and POIs before all hell breaks loose and you're forced to leave is something i really like in concept... and then the Corespawn waves begin and suddenly you're out of time and got barely anything done. To be clear, i have zero issue with not getting everything done all the time and i like to adapt on the fly very much AND the existence of waves themselves aren't even at fault here, it's the way they get distributed. Once you reach the first wave threshold of a level, another wave immediately announces itself on the time indicator while the current one is still in progress and by the time you're done, half the time until the next one has already passed. Having these distractions is fine, but once caves get bigger and the ever increasing ammo shortage sets in, you barely get anything done anymore. It has come to the point where we rarely bother with Exponite veins anymore, just try to speedrun the levels and focus on workbenches/bio boosters/machine events. A possible improvement for that, i believe, would be handling incursions similar to DRG bug breaches(and yes, i'm aware that this game isn't supposed to be DRG, fight me): Once a incursion happens, another one shouldn't be pre-announced until the current one is over; we often get two fixed incursions per level anyway, so another system like that shouldn't hurt the experience that much.

[b] Upgrade Negotiation System [/b]

I'm not its biggest fan but also no its biggest hater. I mainly play games solo or with friends and so far we haven't run into any overly horrible situations because of it. A little bit of coordination with your buddys never hurt anyone. HOWEVER i can only imagine how abysmal this can become in public lobbys - and based on what i've read here so far, my worries seemed to be somewhat justified. What i'm trying to say is... i don't really mind as hard but they definitely need to do some kind of overhaul to that system.

[b] Ammo Economy [/b]

It's rough man, it really is and honestly it should be higher on the improvement list. During regular levels, preserving ammo is somewhat manageable if you don't have to deal deal with the second incursion but once you get to the boss stage, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥! I will take my team of 3(me included) for example. On successful runs, the only way for us to beat a gatekeeper goes like this: Step out the elevator -> Try and beat the first timed incursion to the boss room -> Activate the boss so we don't have to deal with a wave that WILL burn through our reserves and WILL doom the run if we don't prevent it. Not only is there no boss health scaling based on how many are in the team, they are really just huge bullet sponges through and through. Every time on a winning run we had to LITERALLY use ever single resource in the entire cave to barely kill it and wasting any more ammo on other distractions, like incursions, the game expects us to deal with would make this straight up impossible, even with our high tier upgrades. Roguelites are supposed to be tough and get a bit more manageable down the line once you deck yourself out, but this simply isn't the case here somehow. 

Now, what do i think should be prioritized? Mhhhhhh... clearly the ammo economy and or enemy health scaling, if that wasn't obvious yet. And i'd want the see the Ramrod expanded, more detailed and more polished... it just feels very empty. It's not much, but that's all i personally want for now.

[b] BUT WAIT, THERE'S MORE!!! [/b] I asked my buddys if they wanted to add anything to this review, so here it is. They told me, and i quote:

"Add grapple hook and add a secondary option instead of upgrades to just get resupplied. Also there is no other gems to mine and I complain that at resupply it does not replenish health 
Also you should be allowed to pick whatever weapon you want instead of it being 1st come first serve"

[b] And [/b]


"As veterans of DRG the (2) types of ammo crates one for your armor (aka) shield and one for ammo is annoying they slows gameplay 
Management wouldn’t be please there are now (2) things to look for and stop and interact with.
Also would having multiples of the shame character be that op…let people play the character they won’t not be forced to a selection they don’t want"

I can get behind the last one, Rogue Core is literally the Vermintide of DRG games in that regard lmao.
That's about it, hope this gave some sort of insight of the current state. If you don't own the game yet and or plan to get it, maaaaaaaybe wait until its a bit further along in development. If one studio can make this the greatest it can be, its GSG!

[b] Bonus: [/b] I hope the fact, that our first run ended because of a cave leech and no one had ammo left to shoot it, mildly entertains you D;

[h1] A swing and a miss... this Expenite isn't going to mine itself. [/h1]

So like, my review is going to say that I don't recommend this game but I genuinely wish Steam had a mixed category because it's one of those situations where I don't think the game is good enough to justify paying for... YET.

The Devs have acknowledged the three main areas of critique:
The Timer.
The upgrade "negotiation" system.
And.
The ammo economy.

They have also taken VERY small steps to remedy these critiques but have admitted that changing three systems that are effectively load bearing for the entire gameplay loop is going to take time. I, however, reject this idea. There are at least a few things they could do right now to, at the very least, negate some of the issues players are having even today. First and foremost I think the timer could be removed entirely and simply have Corespawn waves attack every 10 minutes or so, a la the assault system from the Payday series. Secondly I think they could increase the amount of ammo shuttles laying around the environment and guarantee one by every single elevator, both entrance and exit.

This is to say that 2.5 of the reasons above are my exact gripes with the game, plus some others. 

Yes, the timer sucks, make it work like Payday instead. I saw a post on Facebook the other day showing indie developers a wheel and begging them not to reinvent it. This game, I think, is the most guilty of that crime at this particular moment. 

Yes, the ammo economy sucks. Even as the Spotter with my co-op duo as the Defender/Tank, we frequently ran out of ammo and usually ended waves with a handful of rounds left each. Contrary to intuition - instead of high fiving with a freeze frame "Yeah we did it!" moment - we immediately got back to our minimum wage slogging, just praying that we found ammo or a supply pod somewhere and soon. I think it is CRIMINAL that the Spotter's Ammo Drop ability doesn't passively recharge. Like, it is limited to being restored when you use a supply pod? My reward for not finding ammo is having even less ammo? Feast or famine game design absolutely sucks and this game demonstrates that with poetic elegance.

Now, you'll notice I said 2.5 reasons above. This is because I don't personally have an issue with the upgrade negotiation system. However, this is because I don't play with randoms. I play with friends in a Discord call. I've never had someone take "the upgrade I want" because I'm not a 12 year old. We actually just discuss upgrades and all agree that the person with a particular build should get a particular perk and sometimes someone just gets the health upgrade. It happens. However, if I did play with internet randoms I'm sure this system would have me frothing at the mouth because what were they thinking? Gunfire Reborn and Far Far West both do this exact system way better. Just drop upgrade cards that are instanced and if you don't like yours then you can ping it to make it available for another player and negotiate that way. 

Something, something reinventing the wheel. 

Forcing players to effectively draw straws for upgrades will ONLY lead to butthurt and rage-quitting. Let players negotiate on their terms, not yours. Yes I realise that there is some DRG flavour to how we get upgrades currently but I'm very confident the devs could make a card exchange system work in the Dwarven context. Have them be upgrade chips the Reclaimers slot into their armour or something? 

Now, I want to address something else. I totally understand there is a lore reason why we can't stack classes... OH WAIT YOU CAN DO IT IN REGULAR DRG! Let us stack classes oh my god. Half of them aren't even that good, stop making us negotiate for these things. "Erm I wanna play Falconer, I had to play Striker last round and I don't like his kit" sucks to be that guy I guess because the classes are already locked in. I'm grateful that there are five classes so that player four isn't just forced to take a certain class or playstyle but it can definitely evoke the feeling of deciding whether you'd like to be punched in the ribs vs kicked in the balls. This game needs way more classes, like way way more, like Risk of Rain 2 more (a game that allows stacking characters by the way).

So, like, I was willing to give the developers the benefit of the doubt, until I learned that a lot of the biggest critiques of the game so far already brought up from the multiple pre-alpha playtests and just fell on totally deaf ears. It feels very cynical to mention that these points of contention are not being taken seriously until they potentially affect the bottom line but that's exactly what is being demonstrate so how cynical is it?

I will file this game under - "come back in 6 months to a year and then decide if it is trash at that point" because frankly this cake is underbaked. It is sagging in the middle and the pâtissier forgot the flavour. I'm confident that Ghost Ship can turn this game around because DRG is literally one of the gaming industry's biggest darlings. But right now they need to sit down and learn from their peers. DRG did so well because no one was quite like it, DRG:RC is doing poorly because it tried to steal DNA from elsewhere and only managed to harvest the defects.

Oh and the way you get cosmetics sucks, there was nothing wrong with how it worked in DRG.

Guys didn't cook this time.

Flat, lineral levels.
Boring, predictible synergies, "statslop" upgrades. "+20 fire on enemies with fire"
One biome, three enemy types.

~1k hours in DRG and more in DRG:S. This is a good start, but I agree that the timer and ammo restraints can be a bit  challenging. Playing with randoms must be tough in terms of negotiation, luckily I play with friends only.
Edit: a few days later nopes, this is not even early access. This is a game looking and feeling like DRG that's not DRG, but I don't know what it is right now.
Edit 2: I managed to play 16 hours with painstaking determination. In the beginning, I had faith this can be turned into a good game, but at this point I feel the entire game would have to be reworked into something different. I guess this is supposed to be a fast-paced roguelite... but the fight itself is just not very enjoyable. Neither are the negotiations (not even after the patch, which indeed improved it). Or the fact that you can get all the expenite you want, but in the end it doesn't all matter that much.
Edit 3: Stuck at 17 hours. I'm not planning to even try playing this unless I hear everything has changed. I've gone back playing good old DRG, which is a gem. No idea why the devs thought this would be a good idea. I don't question their intentions, but this is just a really bad game at this point.

I want to like it, but it needs a few reworks. 

1. Timer is slightly too restrictive for new players at the lowest difficulty. Playing with randos at low level, players are distracted and learning where they should be and what they're doing. Getting overwhelmed while trying to learn how to interact with a point of interest or when is best to start an objective will start player fights and push learning players away.

2. Incentives for cooperation are too low or have low visibility. "Get a benefit for being near other players" skills shouldn't be Epic rarity. There should be a small reward for taking lower-rarity offerings so your teammates can have better choices. There should be more meta-progression perks with benefits to allies as well. Abilities with area effects like Guardian's shield repair have low visual impact and don't encourage grouping up (Gunner's Bubble Shield was fantastic, why did they backslide?).

3. Split-second communication is more important than in DRG, but unless you're on a mic, you're at a severe disadvantage. Pings should live somewhere in the UI so confused players can't so easily miss "There's ammo here" "We should start this objective" "We need to get to the elevator" messages. Left 4 Dead made it easy to read important pings from afar nearly 20 years ago, why is this still happening?

4. Ammo is way too scarce when you can't call down an ammo drop in an emergency. Tweak the numbers, please.

Many other reviews already cover the big problems. The timer makes the game much less fun. The upgrade negotiations interrupt the pace, and are often frustrating. But some things I like. The new player classes and abilities are fun. I like the new enemies.

One issue I don't see a lot of other reviews mentioning is the cave generation. It looks like they are randomly generated, but ultimately, progress through them is linear. You enter at one end, go through the middle to upgrade your weapons, then exit at the other end (either elevator or boss). The environment is destructible, but there's really no reason for it to be. Furthermore, the caves feel really small and cramped. Could they be opened up and expanded somewhat? And though there are lots of different ways to gather expenite, ultimately every mission run feels pretty much the same. Enter, get the green stuff, get better weapons, exit. It gets boring pretty fast.

But here's the real killer for me, and why I have to give a thumbs-down for now. I understand this is not DRG 2. But there is one thing that Ghost Ship MUST bring over from DRG to Rogue Core. The game must allow for emergent and unexpected conditions that require creative solutions to win the mission. That's the secret sauce that made DRG a hit. In DRG, every mission feels different, not because we're given more weapons or enemies or events. It's because the game design itself does not impose a lot of restrictions on how we win a mission. That's why we keep playing it (3,000 hours in my case). The current problem with Rogue Core is that the rules of the game are too constraining to allow for that sort of gameplay. Ghost Ship has to fix that more than anything else, or I'm pretty sure Rogue Core will just get lost in the sea of "good, but not great" games here on Steam and pretty soon be forgotten.

Good luck Ghost Ship, I hope you can turn Rogue Core around and make it another hit!

I've seen a lot of people posting paragraphs-long reviews for this game to hate on it and compare it directly to Deep Rock Galactic, saying "oh this game sucks because its too hard, or its not being balanced, or they don't like the shared upgrade systems". The thing that I'm seeing with all of these is that they're seeing this expecting it to be some DRG 2. They want to easily win every mission, and always have ample ammo and health, but this is ignoring the entire point and theme of the game. The idea behind this game is that the Deep Rock Galactic company dug too deep and everything is either about to come crashing down or already has. 

     Of course you're not going to have perfect stock of ammo and health, you're on a combat team who has to go into a planet that is very much not happy about the exploitation of its resources. You're using the leftover scraps of ammo and materials left behind by you and the company in the last game. The people talking about the shared upgrades and how there's no guarantee you get what you want also miss that this is a game based around teamwork and communication. Maybe you don't see that your teammate will get way more usage out if it than you would. The teamwork aspect of this game is one of the main selling points in both DRG and RC. If you're playing with friends it's funny to take their upgrade, or to shoot them in the back sometimes. I personally am not a fan of people who take games way too seriously, this game was not meant to be won 100% of the time, so have some fun while you're playing. The caves are dark but you don't have to be, lighten up.

Pros:
1. The devs have very much achieved what they wanted. It reads and plays very clearly as a fast-paced, very difficult roguelike that forces you to make hard decisions on your resources, both ammo and time being very important to ensure you never run out of either.

2. Wide selection of options - There's plenty of choices, at least in weapons and characters, with grenades being more limited and equipment even more so, unless you go out of your way to get an equipment crate, with entirely new options up for grabs.

3. Classes are fairly deep and each have their own unique playstyles and build choices despite only really having 3 actives and a passive to separate them. (bio-booster decks too initially but you can unlock the option to swap them out anyways.)

4. Decent range of enemies (on paper).

5. Coop is fairly equal and I have rarely found people taking what I want to take, at least for upgrades.

Cons:
1. Some things are out of your control or are otherwise extremely difficult to plan around (like trying to get something done without having it take way too long since you don't have the right tool.), especially with randoms. While I won't say much about the timer, i understand it's purpose and I feel if you don't take too much time lollygagging you can leave right when the worms arrive, only occasionally missing something that might've spawned in a terrible spot.

2. Wildly ranging weapon feel. Some weapons are great straight out of the tin and can work on a variety of builds easily, some have too little ammo or damage to really doo much. for example, some weapons can kill the same target in a teenth of the time and ammo pool, for no real cost outside of getting lucky enough to get them in the first place.

3. Enemies can feel tanky as ♥♥♥♥ (not even counting the bosses). Even getting full headshots or armor breaking, without focus fire from other teammates or a spotter crit dart, nearly every weapon requires like 2 magazines of ammo to actually kill anything bigger than a creeper, of which also feel quite tanky individually without headshots.

4. Solo is nigh-impossible outside of the easiest difficulty, if not for the sheer ammo required to kill everything but simply just the fact you only have one (and cooper but still) set of hands to do things around the cave, with one option for traversal equipment.

5. Dealing with damage. Armor is either completely full or empty, no in between. And if there isnt at least like 3-4 red sugar producing upgrades in the team, the damage each enemy does, along with how easy they can drown you in units (since you don't have anything to crowd control outside of fairly ineffective grenades), will ensure that you simply cannot outheal the damage dealt by everything.

also why can't we upgrade our equipment? what you get at the start is the only thing you're getting until either an equipment crate (unlikely in a run since the other options are usually better, and you're only taking it anyways because what you currently have sucks ass) or mission end.

tl;dr 
like 8/10-high 7/10 even considering early access, some frustrating aspects but it works well if you put some elbow grease into it. at least it runs well on my midrange PC with next to no bugs and the devs seem eager for feedback. (they've already bulletpointed the issues on ammo economy, timer restrictions, and shared upgrade system, so I imagine changes soon.)

Great game so far. A lot of people seem to be complaining about the same three things. I see where they are coming from, but completely disagree. These are: shared upgrades, timer, and ammo economy.

Shared upgrades: You should not be able to brute force the same build run after run. One of the most important things about rogue-lites is randomness. Saying you don't like that somebody else picked your upgrade? Well, too bad. It's part of the game and adds to the random experience, which is a fun and core component of the genre.

Timer: IT IS A DIFFICULT GAME. If you are not efficient, you will be penalized. The timer is there to keep things moving along at a respectable pace. Some of these missions are already lasting well past 45 minutes and up to an hour and 15. The timer is there to keep things fun, fluid, and fast.

In its current state, I don't think it deserves the name Deep Rock Galactic, nor the label "roguelite." Let’s dissect this:

It’s nothing like DRG; it only shares the graphics. A lot of people have mentioned that this game lacks the teamwork the original had, and I agree, but its not just that, you don't really need to cooperate between you more than I have armor here or the upgrades, in DRG you had to cooperate a lot, specially in higher difficulties, but i feel i can just run alone in this  game.

 While I understand that lore-wise we aren't miners, the mining in this game feels like an afterthought. We only mine one ore? What’s the point of Expenite then? They could just make it so you level up by killing; it would be more integrated. I’m not saying I necessarily want that, but is the point of the pickaxe just to break some terrain and collect Expenite? Let's be real: who is mining a tunnel with their pickaxe? Furthermore, in DRG, you mined for more than just minerals—there were gems in the walls, eggs, or missions where you might need to tunnel for pipes. Here, what is the point?

I also don’t think it functions well as a roguelite. Well, it is one, but not a fun one. There are barely any upgrades; I did four runs, and all of them were repetitive. I tried different builds every time, but the upgrades just aren't significant enough. The biggest change I experienced was an upgrade that left poison behind me, so I just ran everywhere, but there’s barely any synergy in the upgrades either. There aren't enough upgrades per run to make a real change. For example, Risk of Rain 2 upgrades are really bland on their own, but you get maybe 20 per map. Here, it’s like 20 per run; they just don’t feel like they matter. If the point of them is just to buff my health, wouldn't it be more fun to just play DRG? It’s a complete game at the end of the day.

The guns also lack variety, and the abilities are underwhelming; they have too much cooldown, or they are just underpowered. Sure, you can upgrade them, but it’s once per map, and it’s always a choice between upgrading your ability (which has a long cooldown) or your primary source of damage. What would you choose? DRG actually has a much stronger "roguelite" feeling, not because you change your build during the run, but because the same character can feel so different. We have passives like "revive for 30 seconds upon death" in the original, why isn't that here? And the platform gun had upgrades like making enemies avoid stepping on them or negating fall damage, here there's nothing like that...

Lastly, it’s just not fun. While I was playing, I kept thinking I’d rather be playing DRG. The runs are repetitive and the missions are basically the same. Honestly, I don’t feel like the procedural generation is even needed because I’m just shooting—I'm just running around. It could be the same map every time, and I'd just be shooting, you know? I know it’s in Early Access and maybe I haven’t played enough, but I don’t think they are fixing any of this. I’ve already read the roadmap, and it doesn't fix any of these pain points, in my opinion. Maybe in a year, this game will be what I want it to be, but I don’t have high hopes.

I love DRG and have played 590 hours of it and 130 hours of survivor. I was really looking forward to Rogue Core.
- The atmosphere of DRG is still there.
- The hub is pretty cool, but it feels empty and lifeless. It’s also way too rough around the edges. There are literally hallways and doors that lead into dead ends and walls, while the lower floors are a complete maze. I get that it’s Early Access, but couldn’t they at least polish it a little?
- Mission selection is less convenient now. Instead of the simple global map from the original game, you now have to spin around a 3D planet like an idiot trying to find the biome you need.
- I liked the dwarf classes. Just like in the original, at first none of them really feel right, but after spending some time with them and learning how they work, they start becoming fun.
- About the timer: I don’t think it should be removed completely, otherwise the game would just become original DRG with a single resource. I actually like that it pressures you and forces quick decisions — should you keep upgrading or call the elevator already.But because it’s not a proper numerical timer and instead just a vague progress bar, it’s hard to manage, while the punishment is instakill worms.
I’m fine with the idea of “you ran out of time, you lose,” but if you’re expected to call the elevator before the worms appear, then I honestly have no idea how you’re supposed to do anything else. Sometimes the procedural generation places rooms extremely far from the elevator, and a quarter of the timer gets wasted just checking what’s there.
Personally, I think a better solution would be an endless scaling wave and worms that can actually be killed and that don’t appear so quickly. That way, if the team is willing to spend ammo, they could choose to stay longer on a level.
-And most importantly, the upgrades feel very strangely balanced.
Weapon upgrades are almost never worth the time spent getting them.
Character upgrades don’t take your current build into account at all. There are no real upgrade paths, yet you can still get reload speed bonuses when your weapon doesn’t even reload.
Considering the possibilities from the original game, I expected far more elemental mechanics and interesting build options overall. There are barely any synergies. Very rarely can you put together a build where your character actually feels stronger, or even comparable to the original DRG characters.
- The bosses are cool, but again, the problem is that you can end up with a crowd-clearing or melee-focused build and then get completely destroyed by a boss fight.
- And the metaprogression barely feels meaningful. Sure, you level up upgrade trees, but what’s the point if you don’t even end up taking the things you upgraded?
Personally, I think it would be better if you unlocked a perk first and then gradually invested chips into it to increase its effect over time. Instead of going from 8% extra ammo to 12% after six hours of playtime.And considering you can stack multiple copies of the same perk, it ends up going from 8% to 20% after several hours, which feels too sudden. The progression should probably be smoother.
-The price was honestly surprising to me. I don’t understand why an extremely unfinished and empty Early Access game costs the same as the original game, which already has a massive amount of content.Of course, that’s everyone’s personal choice, and “if you don’t like it, don’t buy it,” but there are plenty of fully finished roguelite shooters that cost significantly less.
-It's hard to say about optimization, since my computer is already outdated for modern games. I can say that the original game runs great on maximum settings, and this one runs well on minimum settings with anti-aliasing, but there's not much of a visual difference.

I genuinely hope the developers improve the game over time, but what worries me is that there was already a full year of playtests, and people were complaining about these exact same problems a year ago.
Overall, the game is still far too unfinished. Even though I personally like it, I can’t recommend it to anyone in its current state.

In the original DRG, you could basically stick around as long as you like because the goal is to basically mine everything in sight alongside the original mission objectives. You were encouraged to look around every nook and cranny in hunt for the minerals and resources. In rogue core, the planet is literally trying to kill you! You are trespassing in its domain so it makes sense to me that you are on the clock since hoxxes is doing all it can to eliminate you. You are not there to mine and explore but trying to get to the exfil as quick as you can (like left 4 deads safe rooms almost) and the timer provides that outside pressure perfectly. I played this with my friends and it taught us to prioritize objectives and weigh if we had enough time to complete optional side points of interest. Do you stick around to mine the upgrade resources around you or push forward to find more defensible ground before the next horde arrives? We definitely felt like a team weighing these decisions collectively which is something unique that I really appreciated.

In regards to the upgrades and having to negotiate, I actually enjoy this mechanic as well. I can see with randoms that could be an issue if you are playing with someone whom is selfish and just griefs or robs others of good upgrades, but amongst friends its definitely fun brain storming what would be best for someone's build. It allows you to talk things out with each other in the negotiation and lets you work your brain to make everyone's build optimized. I can still see this being a hit or miss mechanic though. My feedback for that would be to have a potential toggle for this option in lobby matchmaking so people could have the option and otherwise just instance everything to everyone individually. As someone who absolutely loved the original DRG, it’s disappointing to say that Rogue Core feels far too unfinished for an Early Access launch. The core gameplay loop is still addictive and there’s definitely potential here, but the game currently feels more like an unpolished expansion than a fully new experience.

The roguelike systems are very shallow at the moment. Most upgrades are simple stat boosts and rarely lead to interesting or game-changing builds. Combat also lacks impact — enemies barely react to hits, damage feedback is weak, and deaths can feel sudden and frustrating.

Balance is another major issue. Runs can easily be ruined by bad RNG, bosses feel excessively tanky, ammo is too limited, and solo play is unnecessarily punishing. Co-op also lost a lot of the strong class synergy that made the original DRG so fun, mostly because of the shared upgrade system.

On top of that, the game feels oddly empty and unfinished. The hub area is lifeless, maps can be confusing to navigate, and many mechanics are poorly explained for new players. Some control decisions also feel awkward during intense fights.

There’s still a strong foundation underneath all these issues, and I genuinely think the game could become great after enough updates. But in its current state — with bugs, crashes, lack of content, and Day 1 paid cosmetics — it’s very hard to recommend at this price.

For now, I’d say: wishlist it and come back later.

20 hours EA review
It's not DRG 2. But it still rocks the stone.
Roguelite gameplay is fun and challenging, "negotiation" mechanic of picking weapons and upgrades spices things up, mission timer makes every second count and punishes greed.
The game is drastically different from the old DRG in every aspect other than flavor and lore, with much faster pace, higher focus on combat and smaller on exploration. Same time, same place, but different crew for different task. Still can get wasted at the bar or dance all night long though.

I’ve enjoyed the game so far, but there are some incredibly annoying issues that make me want to refund it at times.

The biggest problem is that the game is extremely buggy. Abilities sometimes do not work, weapons and grenades can get stuck and refuse to fire, and these bugs can completely ruin a run. What pushed me to leave a negative review was getting an equipment crate with turrets, only to be unable to place them at all, even between stages. That ended up costing me the entire run.

There are also several gameplay and design issues that need improvement:

1. The UI is awful. It feels overly serious, the text is tiny, and the ascension frames look ugly. A lot of modern games seem to be getting worse with UI design, and this one is no exception.

2. The timer is more frustrating than fun. I understand that it is meant to add pressure, but some weapons feel completely unbalanced. By the time you kill one wave, another one spawns, making exploration nearly impossible.

3. Co-op needs better group mechanics. Players should not have to manually regroup just to upgrade. The upgrade screen should pop up for everyone automatically. Right now, you lose a lot of time just running back to Molly to upgrade together.

4. Upgrade perks feel weak and inconsistent. Most perks barely give any noticeable damage improvement unless you happen to get a broken combination. If you get unlucky, the run can feel doomed no matter how well you play. Right now, it does not feel difficult in a satisfying way, it feels like there is too little skill expression or player impact.

I will keep trying to enjoy and play the game, but I really hope the developers fix the game-breaking bugs and improve some of the core gameplay systems.
